title: Collection and analysis handoff
description: Milestone 4: downstream collection tool spec + analysis-layer relative health score.

title: Collection tool spec
description: Spec a downstream tool that gathers results/*.json from fleet hosts (rsync/scp/robocopy). Skip *.partial files. Retention policy (delete after successful ingestion vs leave to periodic cleanup). Out of scope for this repo, but spec lives here.

title: Analysis-layer relative health score
description: Per-suite-version relative score (z-score or median ratio) vs same-hardware-class peers. Computed from stored raw timings; recomputable when formula changes. Tagged with cpu_suite_version. Not part of collector or runner.

title: Collector v0 (cpu-v0 suite)
description: Milestone 1: Rust collector emitting cpu-v0 results with environment block. See docs/fleetbench_design_v2.md.

title: Scaffold collector/ Cargo project + CLI skeleton
description: Create collector/ Cargo crate. Add clap with subcommands (inspect, cpu). Wire --json flag. Stub out commands so binary builds and runs.
close_reason: Scaffold complete: cargo project builds, fleetbench/inspect/cpu CLI subcommands parse with documented flags, stubs in place for inspect.rs and cpu.rs

title: cpu command: mode/limit/iterations/threads/json flags
description: Wire --mode quick|normal|long with documented presets. --limit, --iterations, --threads override mode defaults. --json emits the full v2 envelope. Mode presets are part of the suite version.
close_reason: cpu command implemented in src/cpu.rs. Mode presets (quick/normal/long) match design doc. --limit/--iterations/--threads override mode defaults; 'auto' resolves to logical CPU count. Builds full v2 Output envelope (status, host, cpu, config, results) using the existing sieve workloads. Correctness failures produce status=failed + ErrorInfo and propagate to exit code 2. Smoke-tested: quick mode runs end-to-end in ~30ms on this host; bad --threads is rejected with a clear message. 4 new unit tests; 18 total.

title: Failure JSON output + exit codes
description: On failure with --json: emit status=failed, error.{kind,message}. Exit 0 success, 1 invalid args/runtime, 2 correctness check failed. Still valid JSON on stdout.
close_reason: Failure JSON path complete. cpu::run() always emits a v2 envelope even on failure, including host/cpu metadata and a populated error block. Argument errors (e.g. --threads 0) now produce status=failed with kind=invalid_arguments rather than a stderr-only message; --json honors the design contract. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 invalid_arguments/runtime, 2 correctness_check_failed. Mapping extracted to exit_code_for() and unit-tested. Smoke-verified that bad args with --json emit a well-formed failure envelope and exit 1.

title: Cross-platform build and smoke test
description: Build Linux and Windows binaries. Run inspect and cpu --mode quick on one representative host per platform. Confirm JSON schema stability and runtime fits in fleet collection window.
close_reason: Cross-platform build + Linux smoke test passed on t-linux64-ms-005 (Ubuntu 18.04, Xeon E3-1585L v5). Static musl x86_64 binary (1.1 MB) cross-compiled from Apple Silicon via cargo-zigbuild and scp'd to target host. smoke.sh validates: inspect (human + JSON), cpu --mode quick (timed + JSON schema validation), cpu --mode normal (timed), failure path with --json envelope. Real-world timings: quick ~0.45s wall, normal ~1.8s wall — well inside the 10-minute runner backstop. Schema v2 confirmed end-to-end, all 3 env slots populated with non-null cpu_percent and load averages, prime_count validates against known pi(10^7)=664579.

title: Bump warmup_prime_limit from 10^7 to 10^8
description: Smoke testing on Xeon E3-1585L v5 (slow x86 fleet host) showed iter 0 still ~20% slower than iters 1-2 in both 1t and mt paths, indicating the governor was still ramping after warmup. At 10^7 warmup completes in ~17ms on this class of host — not enough to fully ramp from idle. Bump WARMUP_PRIME_LIMIT to 10^8 (~170ms on slow x86, ~10ms on fast hosts) to bridge the full idle-to-load transition before timed runs.
close_reason: WARMUP_PRIME_LIMIT bumped from 10_000_000 to 100_000_000. On slow x86 hosts this gives ~170 ms of sustained CPU work to fully ramp the governor before timed runs; fast hosts trade <10 ms of warmup overhead for a known starting point. Smoke retest on t-linux64-ms-005 pending.

title: Refactor env sampling: raw /proc/stat snapshots instead of computed cpu_percent
description:
Current cpu_percent computation in env.rs sleeps 100ms between two /proc/stat reads. Done three times per cpu run (pre-warmup, pre-timed, post-timed), this 300ms of idle time lets the CPU governor down-clock — observable as a consistent ~17% iter-0 penalty in prime_sieve_1t at normal mode on Xeon E3-1585L v5 even with the 10^8 warmup bump.

Fix: emit raw cpu time counters at each sample point. No sleep. Analysis layer differences any two snapshots to compute CPU% over any window (warmup window, timed window, or subsets).

Schema change: LoadSample.cpu_percent -> LoadSample.cpu_counters { idle_units, iowait_units, total_units, kind }. Bumps schema_version 2 -> 3. Update design v2 doc to reflect new shape.
close_reason: LoadSample.cpu_percent -> LoadSample.cpu_counters (idle_units, iowait_units, total_units, kind). Single /proc/stat read, no sleep, no governor down-clock. Schema bumped 2 -> 3. Design v2 doc updated to reflect the new shape and the rationale (raw-data-first, no in-collector rate computation). Smoke validator updated. 29 tests pass.

title: inspect command: host and CPU metadata collection
description: Implement fleetbench inspect --json. Fields: hostname, os_family, os_version, kernel_version, arch, logical_cpus, physical_cpus, cpu.brand, cpu.vendor, cpu.frequency_mhz. Use sysinfo/num_cpus/hostname crates.
close_reason: inspect command implemented. Collects hostname, os_family, os_version, kernel_version, arch, logical/physical CPU counts, CPU brand/vendor/frequency via sysinfo 0.32 + std::env::consts. Emits v2 schema JSON with --json or human-readable summary. Added chrono for ISO-8601 UTC timestamps. 2 new unit tests; smoke-tested on this host.

title: JSON output schema v2 (envelope + serde types)
description: Define serde structs for the full v2 envelope: schema_version=2, collector_version, cpu_suite_version, timestamp_utc, status, host, cpu, config, environment, results. Single JSON object on stdout.
close_reason: Schema types implemented in src/schema.rs with serde. Covers Output envelope (schema_version=2, status ok/failed), HostInfo, CpuInfo, Config (with warmup fields), Environment with three LoadSample points, Results with prime_sieve_1t/mt, ErrorInfo. Skip-if-none serialization keeps success and failure shapes clean. 3 unit tests verify shape.

title: Environment sampling: cpu_percent on Linux (/proc/stat)
description: Read /proc/stat twice ~100ms apart. Diff idle vs total jiffies. Emit cpu_percent in each load sample. No privileges required.
close_reason: cpu_percent sampled via /proc/stat on Linux: two reads ~100ms apart, diff idle (idle+iowait) vs total jiffies, return busy percentage. cfg-gated to Linux; other platforms return None for cpu_percent. parse_proc_stat_cpu and cpu_percent_from_samples are pure functions, unit-tested with synthetic fixtures (7 new tests). Wired into cpu command: three samples per design doc (pre-warmup, pre-timed, post-timed) populate the Environment block. Pre-warmup and pre-timed samples are taken at adjacent points until the warmup task lands.

title: Environment sampling: cpu_percent on Windows (GetSystemTimes)
description: Call GetSystemTimes twice ~100ms apart. Diff idle/kernel/user tick counts. Emit cpu_percent. No PDH/WMI, no admin.

title: Environment sampling: load_1/5/15 on Linux
description: getloadavg(3) or /proc/loadavg. Emit load_1, load_5, load_15 in each load sample. Null on Windows. processor_queue_length stays null for now (see backlog).
close_reason: load_1/5/15 read from /proc/loadavg on Linux. parse_proc_loadavg is pure (whitespace-split, parse first three fields as f64); cfg-gated for Linux. Non-Linux returns None for all three. 3 new parser tests + updated sample_load expectations test.

title: Warmup framework
description: Run a smaller deterministic workload before timed iterations. Record warmup_enabled and warmup_prime_limit in config. Excluded from results. Pre-warmup and pre-timed env samples both captured.
close_reason: Warmup framework implemented. WARMUP_PRIME_LIMIT=10_000_000 runs both prime_sieve_1t and prime_sieve_mt for one iteration each before timed runs, with full correctness validation. Default is enabled; --no-warmup flag skips it and sets warmup_enabled=false, warmup_prime_limit=null in config. Warmup happens between load_pre_warmup and load_pre_timed env samples per the design doc; warmup failures emit a failure envelope with the post-warmup load duplicated into both pre_timed and post_timed slots. LoadSample now derives Clone.

title: prime_sieve_1t: segmented sieve + correctness check
description: Segmented sieve of Eratosthenes, 32 KB chunks. Base primes up to sqrt(N). Validate against pi(10^7)=664579, pi(10^8)=5761455, pi(10^9)=50847534. Emit per-iteration {seconds, prime_count}.
close_reason: Segmented sieve of Eratosthenes implemented in src/sieve.rs. 32 KB segment size, base primes computed via simple sieve up to sqrt(N). known_pi() table covers limits 10..10^9 for correctness checks. run_1t() handles iteration timing + per-iteration correctness validation, returns Vec<PrimeIteration> or ErrorInfo. 6 unit tests pass including pi(10^7). Release-mode pi(10^7) completes in ~10ms on M4 Pro.

title: prime_sieve_mt: parallel segmented sieve via rayon
description: Parallel segmented sieve. Split target range into chunks, sieve in parallel with fixed worker count. Sum prime counts. Same correctness checks as 1t. Emit threads and per-iteration timings.
close_reason: Parallel segmented sieve in src/sieve.rs. segment_starts split across rayon workers; each worker allocates its own 32 KB scratch buffer and counts primes in its assigned segments independently. Thread count configurable: 0 uses rayon's global pool, otherwise a sized ThreadPool is built and install()-ed. run_mt() handles per-iteration timing + correctness validation, mirroring run_1t. Three new tests verify mt matches st across known limits 10..10^6.

title: CPU suite v1
description: Milestone 3: blake3, zstd, fp_vector, stability_loop workloads. Preserve cpu-v0 behavior.

title: blake3_1t and blake3_mt workloads
description: Hash deterministic in-memory generated data with BLAKE3. Single-thread and multi-thread variants. No disk I/O in timed section. Measures integer/SIMD throughput and parallel scaling.

title: zstd_1t workload
description: Compress deterministic in-memory data with zstd, single thread. Branch-heavy integer work, cache/memory patterns. No file I/O in timed section.

title: fp_vector_1t workload
description: Deterministic FP/vector loop (dot product or small matmul). Single thread. Correctness checked with tolerance, not exact equality. Measures FP/SIMD/FMA throughput.

title: stability_loop workload + summary-stats decision
description: Run a short workload repeatedly, emit all timings. Measures variance, thermal ramp-down, noisy neighbors. Decide here whether median/cov summary belongs in collector output for this specific workload (the v0 'no summary stats' rule may have one exception).

title: Preserve cpu-v0 suite behavior alongside cpu-v1
description: cpu_suite_version selectable. v0 results remain bit-for-bit reproducible after v1 lands. v1 is additive, not a rename.

title: Decide: CPython available on Windows perf hosts?
description: If yes, runner is Python. If no, ship as PyInstaller frozen exe or port runner to Rust. Gates runner language choice. Open question from design v2.

title: Decide: latest.json symlink/copy in results dir
description: Convenient for local inspection but adds a write-ordering concern. Open question from design v2.

title: Decide: processor_queue_length on Windows
description: Implement Windows processor_queue_length in v2 (PDH counter, can be flaky) or defer until there is a concrete analysis use for it. Currently null on both platforms.

title: Decide: redundant runner-side load sample
description: Should runner capture its own load sample just before invoking the collector, as a sanity check against the collector's own pre-warmup sample? Probably not, but worth deciding.
close_reason: Moot: env sampling now emits raw counter snapshots (fleetbench-collector-v0-8ne.14), so there is no duplicate-sample concern between runner and collector.

title: Decide: record scheduling source in envelope
description: Envelope could record systemd unit name / cron line / scheduled task name when discoverable. Useful for debugging missed runs.
close_reason: Moot: trigger is boot/manual under the new operational model; there is no external scheduler unit name to discover.

title: Python runner
description: Milestone 2: runner that wraps the collector and persists results. Operational model: invoked by the worker-startup wrapper before the TC worker boots; self-throttles based on the newest envelope timestamp in the results dir (no separate state). Linux-first; Windows deferred until m2-cpython-windows is answered. Reboot-per-test means many invocations per day — most exit fast as no-ops once --min-interval is satisfied.

title: Scaffold runner/ package
description: Create runner/ directory with package layout, entry point fleetbench-run. Language decided by m2-cpython-windows question.

title: Throttle check: derive last-run from results dir
description: On startup, list results dir and find the newest envelope filename. Parse its embedded UTC timestamp and compare to now() minus --min-interval. If the interval is not yet satisfied, log 'last run was Xh ago, skipping' and exit 0. Otherwise proceed with the run. Counts any envelope file (success or failure) as a run, to avoid burning every reboot retrying on a degraded host. No separate sentinel file — results dir is the single source of truth.

title: Activity pre-flight via gwhc (Linux)
description: Before invoking the collector, query gwhc --json on Linux hosts. If state != IDLE, log the gwhc summary (state, state_description, any non-passing checks, warnings) and exit 0. Defense in depth: the operational model already runs the runner pre-worker-startup, but a manual invocation mid-test would otherwise produce noisy results. Skippable via --skip-activity-check. Non-Linux hosts skip the check silently (gwhc is Linux-only).

title: CLI: --min-interval with duration parsing
description: Parse human-friendly durations on the --min-interval flag: 30m, 1h, 24h, 7d, etc. Reject ambiguous units. Convert internally to a timedelta. Default value: 24h. Used by the throttle check.

title: Update design v2 doc: boot-throttle operational model
description: Rewrite the runner section of docs/fleetbench_design_v2.md to reflect the new operational model: invoked by worker-startup wrapper before TC worker boot, self-throttles based on newest envelope timestamp, gwhc pre-flight, --min-interval CLI arg. Remove the systemd-timer / Task Scheduler examples. Note that --min-interval is a soft lower bound dependent on reboot frequency. Multiple-mode-per-host (different cadences per mode) explicitly listed as future v0.x work.

title: Subprocess invocation + stdout capture
description: Shell out to collector with configured --mode and --json. Capture stdout, stderr, exit code. Do not parse or transform the collector results block.

title: Envelope format (run_id ULID, trigger, timing, exit code)
description: Envelope wraps collector JSON unmodified. Fields: envelope_version, runner_version, run_id (ULID), trigger ('boot' or 'manual'), started_utc, finished_utc, collector_exit_code, collector_output. Collector output preserved bit-for-bit. 'boot' indicates the runner was invoked from the worker-startup wrapper; 'manual' is for ad-hoc operator runs.

title: Atomic write: .partial + os.replace
description: Write envelope to <name>.json.partial, fsync, then atomically rename to <name>.json. Use os.replace (works on Windows; overwrites atomically). Collection tool can safely skip *.partial.

title: Filename scheme
description: <ts>_<host>_<suite>_<run_id>.json. ISO-8601 UTC with : replaced by - (Windows legal). Sortable, globbable, no appended files.

title: Hard-failure handling: non-JSON, panic, stderr capture
description: On non-JSON stdout / parse error / panic / signal kill: still write envelope with collector_output=null, collector_stdout_raw, collector_stderr (both 16 KB cap), collector_output_parse_error, collector_killed_by_runner=false. Runner exits 0; benchmark failure visible inside envelope.

title: Timeout backstop + Linux process group SIGKILL
description: Default 10-minute hard timeout. Launch collector with os.setsid; on timeout send SIGKILL to process group. Set collector_killed_by_runner=true in envelope.

title: Windows Job Object (KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE)
description: Launch collector inside a Job Object with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE. On timeout close the job to kill collector + any descendants atomically. pywin32 or small ctypes wrapper. Set up from day one even though v0 spawns no children.

title: Scheduling docs: systemd timer + Task Scheduler
description: Document example systemd timer unit (Linux) and Windows Task Scheduler XML / schtasks command. Weekly cadence initial target. Runner itself is one-shot; OS does scheduling.
